title: performance-canary-sensitivity-hysteresis-rollout-guards
author: Aisha Patel
description: Implements improved sensitivity tuning and hysteresis-based rollout guards for the performance canary system to reduce noisy/false-positive rollback triggers and allow safer automated rollouts. Motivation: we observed oscillations where small transient latency spikes caused canary rollbacks and blocked deployments. This change adds a configurable sensitivity profile per-metric, a hysteresis window for detection logic, and a rollout guard operator that ties canary duration and severity to automated rollback decisions. Changes include: detection algorithm refactor to support weightable metrics, exponential moving average baseline with configurable alpha, hysteresis state machine with enter/exit thresholds and minimum hold time, a new policy resource that maps sensitivity profiles to routes/models, and UI controls in the observability console for tuning and viewing hysteresis state. The description below covers design, testing, and rollout plan. Design summary: replace the previous threshold-based detector with a Detector class that computes smoothed baselines and emits regression hypotheses with severity scores; Hysteresis layer consumes hypotheses and applies enter/exit thresholds plus minimum hold durations; RolloutGuard reconciles canary results with rollout policies and supports soft-fail (mark degraded) vs hard-fail (immediate rollback) behaviors. Configuration: defaults favor low sensitivity with 3-sample hysteresis and alpha=0.2 to reduce churn; advanced profiles allow higher sensitivity for high-SLO customers. Observability additions: new canary metrics (canary_hypothesis_count, canary_hysteresis_state, canary_severity_score) and dashboard panels, plus tracing hooks for detection decisions. Testing: added unit tests for Detector edge cases (cold-start, missing data), hysteresis hold semantics, and end-to-end perf-canary integration tests using the perf lab harness to validate that transient 200ms spikes do not trigger rollback while sustained regressions do. CI: initial flake in integration test was fixed by increasing test harness timing tolerances; all CI checks passing on final run. Rollout: gated rollout via feature flag and staged rollout to infra teams for 48 hours, then ramp to 50% of org traffic for 7 days before full rollout. Backout plan: feature flag off reverts to previous detector; in-flight canaries will be marked deprecated and reconciled. Release notes included below.

release_notes: Improves performance canary stability by adding sensitivity profiles and hysteresis-based rollout guards. Reduces false-positive rollback triggers from transient spikes and provides per-customer tuning via the Console. New metrics included: canary_hypothesis_count, canary_hysteresis_state, canary_severity_score. Rollout gated behind feature flag and staged to infra teams first.
